verdicts.reason: Quote states o_tx_ready=1 during reset; checkable every cycle from interface signals.
Quote gives sampling point H=floor(N/2) edges after T0, then every N edges; scenario check.
Quote states o_rx_valid at V=M+2; M is internal (sample edge), but the cycle relation can be checked in scenario/assertion.
Quote states new byte loaded with no overrun in this corner case.
Quote requires a 1-to-0 transition for new start after frame error; break gives one byte.
Quote states synchronizer resets to 1 and low line at release is detected as start.
Quote states outputs hold last values while valid=0 and are 0 after reset; checkable from interface signals every cycle.
Quote: reset during transmission abandons frame, o_txd=1 at once, byte lost; assertion on o_txd plus scenario.

Quote 'Not reported' is a negative requirement, which is a MUST_NOT; but the 'dropped byte' is vague. Strength and check are plausible; the fix is the strength only if it was wrong. Here the rule is MUST_NOT and scenario, so it is correct, but a dropped byte has no observable frame-error flag, so it is ambiguous. Keep MUST_NOT/scenario.
Quote says elaboration error recommended (should), not verified; SHOULD with check none.
Quote states which configurations are simulated and that CFG-MAX is not; scenario-checkable.
Quote states no area budget; area reported not checked; nothing to check.
Quote states the corner for the 50 MHz target; timing is a synthesis matter, not simulated.

questions.question: UL-14-09: what does 'a byte is dropped' mean (overrun when the held byte is not taken?), and how is the frame-error of a dropped byte observed, since the output holds the last loaded values (UL-14-07)?
UL-14-03: M is an internal sample edge; define it relative to the observable i_rxd stop-bit timing (T0 and H) so V=M+2 can be checked at the interface.
UL-14-01 and UL-14-08: is o_tx_ready 1 immediately on reset assertion (asynchronous) or only after the next clock edge? Likewise for o_txd=1 'at once'.
